articles.title: 'Make women feel seen': Why the Dutch have a new word for labia
articles.summary: Campaigners hope the new words will lead to less body shaming and more sex positivity.

blocks.text: 'Make women feel seen': Why the Dutch have a new word for labia

blocks.caption: Image caption, Shari Klein spoke at a recent march celebrating the new word

blocks.text: Image source, Luciano Ölz
Shari Klein spoke at a recent march celebrating the new word
BySmitha Mundasad
Health reporter

Can you imagine seeing the words "shame lips" on your medical notes? The term, which can also be translated as "pubic lips", is the Dutch word for a women's body part. But, for some, it's just one of countless examples that are outdated and loaded with stigma.
Last month, leading Dutch dictionary Dikke van Dale said it would include a new term for the labia, "vulvalippen" - in its upcoming online addition - alongside the traditional term "schaamlippen".

European campaigners have long been calling for a rewrite of terms used to discuss women's bodies, sexuality and health. What unites them is the desire to move away from terms that are often seen as misogynistic or judgmental.
"Language shapes how we see ourselves," says Shari Klein, one of the founders of the Schaamteloos campaign, which targets words that use "schaam" or "shame".
"It's crucial people have a more neutral, anatomically correct word - not a word that links to shame, whether consciously or sub-consciously," she says.
'Sex positivity'
Calls to use vulvalippen aren't new but campaigners say inclusion in the dictionary may be a sign society is "finally ready for change".
Esther Van der Valk, part of prominent Dutch feminist group Dolle Mina, says it's also about sex positivity and reducing body shaming.
The campaign's next steps are to convince doctors and officials to use vulvalippen in leaflets and consultations.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Signs used during a recent march in the Netherlands, the one on the left translates as "afterall there are no shame balls"

blocks.text: Signs used during a recent march in the Netherlands, the one on the left translates as "afterall there are no shame balls"

Ton den Boon, editor of the dictionary, says adding vulvalippen is justified because it is becoming more established in the language and is being used more in the media, biology text books, medical leaflets and is even seen in veterinary medicine.
But whether it will be adopted widely is yet to be seen.

Other Dutch words, relevant to both men and women, could carry similar connotations - from "schaam haar" (pubic or shame hair) or "schaam been" (pubic or shame bone) to even "schaam lice" for pubic lice.
However, critics say changing a word will not necessarily change people's lives.
The campaign mirrors attempts in Germany, where in 2018 journalists Gunda Windmüller and Mithu Sanyal started a petition to change "Shamlippen" to "Vulvalippen".
Windmüller says she was compelled to after a gynaecologist told her of the shame some women carry when discussing their bodies and having medical examinations.
When writing her article, she realised she couldn't even mention anatomy without including the word shame.
"Vulvalippen" has not yet been adopted by a German dictionary, but Windmüller has spotted it in conversations, school textbooks and women's magazines.
Her hope is the Dutch move will ignite support closer to home.
'Virginity membrane'
Similarly, in Sweden a new word for "hymen" was added in the academic dictionary after a 2009 campaign.

The association for sexuality education (RFSU) felt traditional term "mödomshinna", which translates as maidenhood skin or virginity membrane, was anatomically inaccurate and did nothing to dispel myths around hymens and virginity.
The new term "slidkrans" translates as vaginal corona - reflecting the fact the hymen is often folds of tissue in a ring, rather than a seal that breaks once.
"With a new word we can challenge the myths that seek to control women's sexuality and freedom," Sonja Ghaderi of the RFSU says.
Ghaderi says slidkrans is used particularly by healthcare professionals and in youth clinics but adds misinformation still exists emphasising the "need to change social constructs".

blocks.caption: Image caption, Supporters took to the streets in the Netherlands to celebrate and publicise the new word

blocks.text: Supporters took to the streets in the Netherlands to celebrate and publicise the new word
In the UK, feminist podcast host Nicola Denson-Elliott started a petition to replace the word "hysterectomy" (surgical removal of the womb) with "uterectomy".

She argues, as others have, that hysterectomy has linguistic links with hysteria, external - once seen as a disease of emotional excess in women - and wants a more "anatomically correct term" not one "associated with emotion."
The petition describes it as "medical misogyny", adding: "Women deserve terminology that respects them."
'Judgmental words'
Linguistics researcher Dr Beth Malory says any changes need to be researched first.
"Will people understand uterectomy? Is simply saying removal of the womb better?"
New words cannot be ambiguous, she says, it's important to look at the whole system so there is no confusion.
Malory also studies language around pregnancy and loss.

One phrase highlighted in her research is "incompetent cervix" used to describe the shortening of the cervix that can increase risks of pregnancy loss and early birth. Women told her it made them feel blamed for the medical issue.
"Why do we need judgmental words like failure or incompetence?" says obstetrician Dr Brooke Vandermolen, external.
Even though they appear in medical textbooks, she tells me she's moved away from certain terms, including "failure to progress" - which describes labour not moving forward as expected.
"Language is incredibly important and the words we choose can show recognition and make people feel validated and seen."
In 2022, the Royal College of Midwives produced guidance offering alternative phrases.
But Vandermolen says some traditional terms are still being used and still cause distress.
"I hope this change in the Netherlands sparks more conversations here about how we speak about women's bodies. What we say can have a lasting impact."

articles.title: Justin Bieber performs surprise acoustic gig in beleaguered Los Angeles park
articles.summary:
Small crowd enjoys singer’s free concert in MacArthur Park, which has often drawn headlines for less cheery reasons

With no announcement and little fanfare, Justin Bieber

blocks.text: With no announcement and little fanfare, Justin Bieber performed a free acoustic set on Monday at a Los Angeles park often in local headlines for less cheery reasons.

In videos that surfaced online, four musicians flanked the global phenom, who wore a plain T-shirt and shorts as he sang hits including Daisies and Yukon. The low-key affair with a small crowd stood in stark contrast to Bieber’s recent blockbuster World Cup and Coachella performances.
Some online users expressed surprise at the venue choice. A spokesperson for Bieber could not be immediately reached for comment about what spurred the show.

MacArthur Park, located west of downtown Los Angeles, is often described in ominous terms. The area has been plagued by gang activity and rampant drug use. Homeless encampments have also cropped up around the park in recent years.

blocks.caption: A jacaranda tree in MacArthur Park in May. Photograph: Patrick T Fallon/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Earlier this year, federal authorities condemned the park as an “open-air drug market” after arresting several individuals who they accused of trafficking meth and fentanyl on to its grounds.
The park also became a flashpoint in the Los Angeles mayoral race, with mayor Karen Bass’s challengers using it as a benchmark for her progress on public safety.

In June, Bass disavowed crime in the park, saying the Los Angeles police were employing every resource to curtail illicit activity. Bass said the state and county had a role to play in the solution. “They must increase funding for treatment facilities and recovery services to stop the revolving door between jail and our parks,” she said.
Bieber’s performance comes after Los Angeles district attorney Nathan Hochman hosted a picnic at the park, following up on an earlier pledge to make the park family-friendly.
after newsletter promotion
“He’s definitely on the invite list for next year’s Labor Day weekend picnic!” Hochman wrote on X of Bieber.
“Bieber in MacArthur park. That’s progress,” first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli posted on X. “Amazing what can happen when criminals and drug dealers are removed from public spaces.”

articles.title: Bill for social media franchises, DICT content oversight? Not so fast
articles.summary: As the government moves to rein in online platforms after deadly school shootings, HB 4786 risks giving Congress and DICT sweeping power over these

blocks.text: As the government moves to rein in online platforms after deadly school shootings, HB 4786 risks giving Congress and DICT sweeping power over these

items: The Philippine government is responding to recent school shootings by examining the role of online platforms in youth violence, with potential restrictions on platforms like Reddit, Discord, and Facebook.
The SAGIP BATA Act has been passed to penalize the recruitment of children into violent activities and requires online platforms to have local representatives for better cooperation with authorities.

House Bill No. 4786, which would require social media platforms to obtain a congressional franchise to operate in the Philippines, raises concerns about government overreach and potential abuse of power regarding content moderation and free speech.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – After school shootings in Tacloban, Zamboanga, and most recently South Cotabato, the government has been scrambling for answers on the role online platforms may play in exposing young people to violence.

The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) recently gave Reddit and Discord 24 hours to designate a local representative, warning that authorities could restrict or block the platforms if they failed to cooperate, before extending that time limit after meeting with the firms.

A month earlier, following the Zamboanga shooting, the CICC floated a possible Facebook ban. Malacañang said restrictions could be considered, although DICT Secretary Henry Aguda later described blocking Facebook as a “last resort.”

DICT also announced that the House had called Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to appear over social media safety, only to retract that statement days later that no House resolution had actually summoned or invited him.

The Senate, meanwhile, has passed the SAGIP BATA Act on third and final reading on September 21. It penalizes recruiting or inducing children into serious violent activity and has requirements intended to make online platforms more reachable by Philippine authorities. The proposed law would require platforms to designate Philippine-based legal representatives who could receive subpoenas, takedown orders and requests for account information.

The government has also negotiated directly with Meta and Roblox. After meetings in Singapore, they agreed to stronger cooperation on child safety, faster responses to harmful content and lawful requests, while Meta agreed to create a technical working group.
But House Bill No. 4786 or the Social Media Platform Franchise Act raises eyebrows. Here’s why it should raise yours:

Filed in September 2025 by Quezon Representative David “Jay-Jay” Suarez, HB 4786 would require covered social media platforms to obtain a congressional franchise before they could operate in the Philippines.

The proposal has regained attention after the South Cotabato shooting. Malacañang has now called it a “good proposal,” saying it could give the government greater jurisdiction and authority over social media platforms. The DICT has also welcomed it.
Beneficially, it would require covered platforms to establish a registered Philippine entity or branch, appoint a local representative, and provide a grievance mechanism for Filipino users.
But it also gives substantial powers to the government that could be prone to abuse.

It would give the DICT, in coordination with the National Telecommunications Commission, primary regulatory jurisdiction over platform obligations involving content moderation, national security, data protection, complaints and public-service standards.
It places “content moderation” under DICT’s regulatory jurisdiction.

The bill does not spell out in detail what standards would govern that oversight, nor does it clearly answer what happens when DICT and a platform disagree over lawful but controversial speech, or what safeguards would protect journalism, political criticism, satire, or unpopular viewpoints from regulatory pressure.

Suppose those questions would be settled in the implementing rules and regulations. Nevertheless, it would still echo concerns already raised over the House’s anti-disinformation bill, which has been criticized by rights advocates and opposition lawmakers who warned that concepts such as public harm and national security as they relate to online content could still be applied too broadly.
With the bill, you’re giving power to a government body for regulating speech in social media.
And the bill would require a legislative franchise, meaning platforms would need Congress to authorize its continued operation.

The Philippines has already seen how politically charged a franchise process can become: In 2020, a House committee rejected ABS-CBN’s bid for a fresh franchise, driven by the grievances of then-president Rodrigo Duterte, creating a massive chilling effect for the media — and our democracy was all the worse for it.
Who wants to extend that system, or simply put, that power to the platforms where much of modern public discourse now takes place? Who really benefits?
HB 4786 would not apply only to today’s tech giants.

The bill defines a social media platform broadly as a service centered on user-generated content, communication and interaction. The eventual implementing rules would determine the user threshold at which a platform becomes covered.

That means a Filipino entrepreneur could build an alternative social network, grow it successfully, and eventually find that continued operation depends on obtaining a franchise from politicians, subject to the same whims.

Requiring local representatives, establishing emergency-response procedures, punishing people who groom children toward violence, enforcing lawful court orders and creating clear duties for platforms are all regulatory approaches already being considered.
So just what exactly do we need a congressional franchise for? – Rappler.com

articles.title: HIV diagnoses drop, but 128,000 Filipinos may be unaware they’re infected
articles.summary: The DOH estimates that 288,000 people in the country are living with HIV

blocks.text: The DOH estimates that 288,000 people in the country are living with HIV

items: HIV diagnoses in the Philippines dropped by 39% in Q2 2026, with 2,994 new cases reported, but many remain unaware of their status.
Approximately 288,000 people are living with HIV in the country, with 128,000 potentially undiagnosed, highlighting the need for improved testing and care access.
The forum emphasized the importance of local AIDS councils, community organizations, and youth education to enhance awareness and treatment adherence.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
BAGUIO, Philippines – The number of HIV diagnoses reported in the Philippines fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026.
But at a forum held in Baguio City on September 17, health workers and community advocates turned to a harder question: How do you reach people who have never been tested?

The Department of Health (DOH) recorded 2,994 new diagnoses from April to June, down 39% from the same period in 2025. That is a count of people diagnosed, not necessarily people who acquired HIV during those three months. Fewer reported diagnoses alone cannot establish that fewer infections occurred.
The DOH estimates that 288,000 people in the country are living with HIV. As of June, 159,997, or 56%, had been diagnosed. The gap suggests that about 128,000 people may be unaware of their status.

blocks.caption: [OPINION] The HIV epidemic we saw coming — and can still stop

blocks.text: The figures drove the first HIV Watch Media Conference, organized by AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) Philippines in Baguio City. National and local health officials, youth representatives, and organizations led by people living with HIV discussed how to turn the quarterly report into better access to testing and care.

“Every quarter, important HIV data becomes available,” said AHF Philippines country program manager Dr. Ryan Guinaran. “Our challenge is ensuring that these numbers lead to concrete action from government, local leaders, communities, and all sectors involved in the response.”
The gap is visible in the Cordillera. Of an estimated 2,700 people living with HIV in the region, 1,403, or 52%, had been diagnosed, according to the DOH report.
Nationally, 111,154 people were receiving antiretroviral treatment as of June.
The report also listed 32,610 people as lost to follow-up, meaning they had not returned to a treatment facility within 30 days of their expected medicine refill.
The numbers point to two tasks for local health services: helping people learn their status and making it easier for those diagnosed to stay in care.
At the forum, participants called for active local AIDS councils, stronger community organizations, youth-focused education, and a greater role for people living with HIV in decisions about services.

Treatment can control HIV and protect health. Of the people on treatment who received a viral load test in the past 12 months, 97% had a suppressed viral load. But only 59% of those on treatment had such a test recorded during that period, leaving the outcome unknown for many others. A viral load test measures the amount of HIV in the blood and helps show whether treatment is working.
Young people are part of the picture. Those aged 15 to 24 accounted for 918, or 31%, of the quarter’s newly reported diagnoses. People aged 25 to 34 made up the largest group, with 1,294 cases.

There were signs of progress in prevention. The DOH recorded 9,640 new enrollments in pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP, during the quarter, up 10% from the previous three months. PrEP is medication used by people without HIV to reduce their risk. – Rappler.com

articles.title: COA finds control, documentation deficiencies in OVP relief operations
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit (COA) has cited the Office of the Vice President (OVP) over inconsistencies, deviations from guidelines, and missing or incomplete documentation in its relief operations…

blocks.text: The Commission on Audit (COA) has cited the Office of the Vice President (OVP) over inconsistencies, deviations from guidelines, and missing or incomplete documentation in its relief operations involving nearly P168 million in 2025.
In its 273-page report on the 2025 Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (DRRMF), COA identified several deficiencies in the implementation of the OVP’s relief operations.

These included inconsistencies between situational reports, deviations from approved mission orders, the issuance of open-ended mission orders, and deficiencies in beneficiary and distribution records.
COA also noted missing or incomplete documents required to support the relief operations.

In its audit, COA identified inconsistencies between situational reports prepared by concerned agencies and local government units and those prepared by the OVP. The discrepancies involved relief operations covering welfare goods worth P19.67 million, including differences in the reported number of affected families.

State auditors also found that 24 relief operations involving P39.01 million worth of welfare goods deviated from approved Mission Orders without documented approval. The changes involved schedules, distribution locations, quantities of relief items and the amount of rice distributed.

The audit further found that eight Mission Orders covering P84.12 million in relief distributions did not specify target beneficiaries, instead directing the distribution of goods to affected or displaced families.
COA said this lack of defined beneficiary targets weakened the basis for determining the quantities of relief goods requested and distributed.

The audit team also identified deficiencies in beneficiary and distribution records, including uncertified master lists, discrepancies between Relief Distribution Sheets and master lists, incomplete beneficiary information, duplicate entries and unsigned distribution sheets.

In addition, COA said some relief operations used documentary requirements intended for the OVP's Relief for Indigents and Individuals in Crisis and Emergencies program despite being covered by the Disaster Operations Policy Manual.

The audit found that relief operations involving 33,980 beneficiaries and P25.27 million worth of welfare goods lacked complete pre-operation documents, including situational reports, Mission Orders and verified master lists.
In one case, a required Relief Distribution Sheet was unavailable after records were reportedly lost during Typhoon Kristine and was replaced with explanatory and certification documents.
COA said the deficiencies reduced assurance over the completeness, reliability and verifiability of relief distribution records and weakened controls over the OVP's relief operations.

The audit team recommended that the OVP strengthen its review procedures and ensure that operational adjustments, beneficiary lists and distribution records are properly documented, verified and authorized.
It also recommended that future Mission Orders clearly define the scope and coverage of relief operations whenever sufficient information is available during the planning stage.
Vice President Sara Duterte's spokesperson, Atty. Paolo Panelo, said that the OVP will release a statement about the matter after reviewing the COA notice.

"Kakatanggap ko lang ng mga request for comment tungkol diyan at nakikipag-ugnayan pa lang ako ngayong araw sa OVP, kung sino ang puwedeng sumagot dito. Maglalabas naman ng sagot o pahayag ang OVP kapag naaral na nila yung COA notice or letter," Panelo said in an interview on Unang Balita on Thursday.

(I have just received requests for comment regarding that, and I am currently coordinating with the OVP today to determine who can respond to this. The OVP will issue a response or statement once they have studied the COA notice or letter.)

"Kahapon, nung nag-usap kami ang sabi niya, laban tayo attorney. So, hindi siya natitinag, hindi siya magpapatalo sa mga latest development. Alam niyang tumitindig siya sa tama, so tuloy-tuloy lang ang laban," Panelo added.

(Yesterday, when we spoke, she said, 'Let's fight this, Attorney.' She remains undeterred and won't let the latest developments defeat her. She knows she is standing up for what is right, so the fight continues.) —LDF/ VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying
articles.summary: Dopamine sites mimic shopping’s thrill without the spending, turning the ritual of consumption into a digital game.

blocks.text: Image source, Purvansh Parmar
FoodNeverComes calls itself a 'dopamine kitchen'
You are hungry. Or you are not. It doesn't matter.

You open FoodNeverComes, pick from 22 cuisines and start scrolling. Butter chicken looks good. So does bibimbap. You add a few dishes, watch the total climb and hit checkout. A tracker says a rider is on the way.

Then you get a dummy AI-generated call from inside the site. He is outside your building, he says, but cannot find your street or door. Except there was never any food in the first place. The order exists only on the screen.
"Order the food. Skip the bill," says the site., external Its slogan is blunter: "The food never comes - but the dopamine does."

Built by two 26-year-old software developers - Purvansh Parmar and Anshul Sharma - from Udaipur in India's northern state of Rajasthan, FoodNeverComes says it has attracted more than 2.7m visitors since its launch in June.
It now offers 22 kitchens, 327 dishes and 319 real recipes, complete with fake prices, a simulated checkout and a fictional delivery experience.

blocks.caption: Image caption, The site offers 22 fake kitchens, 327 dishes and 319 real recipes

blocks.text: The site offers 22 fake kitchens, 327 dishes and 319 real recipes

FoodNeverComes belongs to a new internet genre: "dopamine sites", which recreate the rituals of consumption without the consumption. There are fake shopping sites, fake delivery services and even fake holidays.

The genre took off in South Korea, external and has since travelled well beyond, spawning a growing crop of sites - Dopamine Shop, external or Fakehaul, external, for example - that mimic everything from food delivery and shopping to travel.
What, exactly, are we enjoying when we enjoy buying something?

The idea began with the founders' own shopping habits. Parmar and Sharma met on a computer science diploma course and later started NeuroX AI, which builds software and AI products and makes Instagram content. They noticed it in their own lives: online baskets filling up with things they wanted, but never actually bought.
Sharma would browse electronics, fill an online basket and abandon it. Parmar's mother did much the same. "She would add things to the cart and say, 'I will order this later'," he recalls.

Parmar's own version ended at food delivery checkouts. During a two-month project in Mumbai, he says, he was spending 5,000-10,000 rupees a week on food, sometimes ordering treats he did not necessarily need: Belgian waffles, ice cream and, once, a large jar of sour cream he barely wanted and gave away to friends.
He believes "perhaps the real craving was not always for the food, but for the ritual of ordering it".

blocks.caption: Image caption, Purvansh Parmar says he spent a lot of money on a work trip on food and treats he did not necessarily need

blocks.text: Purvansh Parmar says he spent a lot of money on a work trip on food and treats he did not necessarily need
What begins as genuine hunger, the two argue, can become associated with the pleasure of ordering. Over time, boredom, anxiety or habit can trigger the urge even when the hunger has disappeared.

"Sometimes you're not hungry at all. You're bored or busy, and then you realise that ordering food makes you feel good. You start associating the act of ordering with that dopamine hit. Eventually, it's not just the food you want," says Parmar.

Ravi Dhar, director of the Yale Center for Customer Insights, calls this "anticipatory utility" - the pleasure of looking forward to consumption. It is especially strong with things that capture the imagination - a new pair of shoes, a holiday, a restaurant meal - because anticipation becomes part of the experience.
Sometimes, Dhar says, anticipation can be more pleasurable than ownership: "The thrill is in the chase." Once the object is acquired and the tension resolved, psychological arousal falls.

Neuroscience has a name for this gap between the chase and the catch, and it complicates a popular idea. Dopamine is not simply the brain's pleasure chemical, whatever the internet's talk of "dopamine hits" might suggest.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Swiggy, a popular food delivery site in India, alone handled roughly 2.5m consumer orders a day in FY2025

blocks.text: Image source, NurPhoto via Getty Images
Swiggy, a popular food delivery site in India, alone handled roughly 2.5m consumer orders a day in FY2025

Kent Berridge, a University of Michigan neuroscientist who developed the theory of "wanting" and "liking", says they are separate processes. Wanting is the motivational pull towards something; liking is the pleasure of having it. They often travel together, but not always. Dopamine, in his account, drives the first, not the second.
Tempting food or products online are likely to activate this wanting system, which Berridge calls "incentive salience".

"Some situations can trigger 'wanting' by itself," he says. We can pursue something intensely even when the eventual pleasure is weak - or, in more everyday terms, want something more than we ultimately like it.
Dr Anna Lembke, a Stanford University addiction psychiatrist and author of Dopamine Nation, makes a similar distinction.
"To call dopamine a chemical of pleasure is an oversimplification," she told me. "Dopamine is the molecule that says 'get more of' or 'do more of', but it doesn't necessarily equate to pleasure."

blocks.caption: Image caption, TripNeverLeaves lets users plan a holiday before sending them on a virtual flight that never leaves the runway.

blocks.text: TripNeverLeaves lets users plan a holiday before sending them on a virtual flight that never leaves the runway.

What she adds is the role of ritual. Cues and habits attached to a reward can become reinforcing in their own right, she says: in addiction, the routines leading up to drug use can eventually matter as much as the drug itself. "Anticipation of reward can be as reinforcing as the reward itself," she says.
Can repeatedly ordering imaginary food satisfy a real craving? Berridge says the ritual could produce a "dopamine hit and strong 'wanting', and also evoke faint conditioned 'liking'".
But he would expect the "novelty to soon wear off", and would be "surprised" if many people returned to place more than about 10 imaginary orders.
Dhar is more open to the possibility that simulated consumption could serve as a kind of release valve.
"While we still need more empirical data to know if simulated shopping can satisfy a consumer urge, evidence from simulated consumption in gaming shows it can be highly effective," he says.

blocks.caption: Image caption, A festive sale of of e-commerce site in India featuring Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
A festive sale of of e-commerce site in India featuring Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan
But there is an equally plausible danger: the ritual may simply rehearse the behaviour it is supposed to replace.

Lembke says the evidence is not in yet, and the effect may depend on the person. But her own bet is that, over time, the sites could "reinforce the same addictive neural networks they are trying to simulate".
"The one up side, though, is that people using these sites have on some level already admitted to themselves they have a problem, and that admission is often the first step in recovery," says Lembke.

Sharma ran an accidental experiment of his own. When his phone screen cracked, he spent a week on Amazon comparing six or seven replacements and adding them to his basket. Then he repaired the handset.
"I enjoyed the process of research and putting the phones in the cart," he says. "Eventually I didn't buy a phone."
He now catches himself doing the same on food delivery sites, particularly when anxious, filling baskets without checking out. "I realised that I suffer from this problem," he says.

blocks.caption: Image caption, TripNeverLeaves lists 260 places 'you won't go'

blocks.text: TripNeverLeaves lists 260 places 'you won't go'
The site's blog explores the "serious side" of the fake takeaway, from food-delivery addiction and why fake ordering feels good to cravings, guilt and the psychology of the shopping cart.

The founders have since taken the idea beyond food. A second site, TripNeverLeaves, lets users plan a holiday - destination, flight, seat, hotel and activities - then sends them on a virtual flight that never leaves the runway. They say it has attracted more than 100,000 visitors.
Who those visitors are is harder to establish. But Lembke says younger people may be especially vulnerable to reinforcing digital rewards because the "developing brain is a vulnerable brain".

"In childhood and early adolescence, the front lobe, which acts like the brakes on appetite, is not yet fully connected to the emotion centres of the brain. Hence, teens are more likely to take risks without appreciating the negative consequences, and more likely to get addicted to reinforcing substances and behaviours, once exposed," she says.
For now, the founders say the sites are not about making money. They plan to keep them free and eventually share the data with neuroscientists and psychologists.
What looks like a joke about ordering too much food has stumbled into a bigger question about modern consumption: if so much of the thrill comes before we get the thing, do we need the thing at all?

articles.title: Tony Blair says Britain should work towards rejoining EU in next 10 years
articles.summary:
Andy Burnham under pressure to revisit Brexit as poll suggests pledge to rejoin could boost Labour’s electoral chances

Britain should work towards rejoining the EU in the next decade, Tony…

blocks.text: Britain should work towards rejoining the EU in the next decade, Tony Blair has said, adding to growing pressure on Andy Burnham to abandon Labour’s reluctance to revisit the 2016 referendum.
The former prime minister has urged Burnham to use his 10-year plan in November to put the country’s membership of the union back on the table, a decade after it voted to leave.
In a paper entitled A Path to Rejoining a Reformed Europe, the Tony Blair Institute (TBI) calls for the UK to accept free movement of people and make a financial contribution as the price of entry.
The intervention comes after Burnham declined to rule out promising to rejoin the EU in the next Labour manifesto, though it also threatens to reopen the deep rifts caused by the vote 10 years ago.

In a foreword to the paper, Blair argues: “Britain should signal an intention if the terms are right to enter into a structured formal relationship with Europe and initiate a process of negotiation where everything is on the table but nothing agreed until everything is agreed.”
TBI researchers say in the paper itself: “Over the next decade, Britain should work towards the ambition of rejoining a significantly reformed EU.”

blocks.caption: Tony Blair speaking at a Board of Peace conference in New York on Wednesday. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/Getty Images

blocks.text: Blair is the latest in a series of Labour figures to back rejoining the EU. Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, has called the Brexit vote a “catastrophic mistake” and said the party should aim to rejoin the bloc, while Burnham himself told the Guardian last year: “I hope in my lifetime I see this country rejoin the European Union.”

But Burnham has said he does not wish to pursue membership of the union in the near term. When asked by reporters this week if it could be in the next election manifesto, he said it was a question “for another day”.

Others are sceptical of the electoral wisdom of giving the appearance that the party wants to undo the result of the 2016 referendum, especially in areas of the country where Reform UK has made inroads in recent years.
Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, dismissed the idea earlier this year as she warned against “reopening the circular arguments that we ended up in as a country”.

However, pollsters suggest Labour could benefit electorally by promising to rejoin. A new megapoll conducted by YouGov on behalf of the pro-EU campaign group Best for Britain suggests the party could more than double its seat total if it goes into the next election promising to rejoin.

The survey of more than 13,000 people, undertaken in June before Burnham became prime minister, found that a pledge to seek membership would help unite progressive voters behind Labour while doing nothing to boost Reform’s vote.
after newsletter promotion

The results suggested the move could take Labour from a projected 136 seats to 321 – though those totals will have changed since Burnham came to office, which has given the party a poll lead for the first time in months.

The TBI paper calls for Britain to try to accelerate European market reforms using possible re-entry as leverage. It argues that pro-reformers in Brussels would have a significant incentive to work with Britain on a project to make the EU more economically liberal and to reform its regulations on energy and technology.

It adds that Burnham should scrap the government’s red lines of not rejoining, not allowing free movement and not entering the single market or a customs union. The paper argues that the prime minister should replace them with a single promise only to sign up to rules and initiatives that prove of economic or strategic benefit to the UK.
TBI has advocated in recent years for the UK to slow down its push to achieve net zero carbon emissions and is a heavy backer of increased use of artificial intelligence in government.

Its policy positions have brought scrutiny on some of the institute’s most high-profile funders, who include the technology billionaire Larry Ellison, and its clients, which include the government of Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Palace defends P58.5-B local fund against 'presidential pork' claim
articles.summary: Palace responds to Rep. Erice, who is threatening an Supreme Court challenge to the proposed P58.53-billion local fund.

blocks.text: September 24, 2026 | 7:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang defended the proposed P58.53-billion Local Government Support Fund for 2027 against a lawmaker's claim that it amounts to a "presidential pork barrel."

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro rejected Caloocan 2nd District Rep. Edgar Erice's characterization of the LGSF as a discretionary fund under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., saying releases to local governments are subject to requirements and evaluation.

Erice has questioned whether Congress is giving the executive too much discretion over which local governments receive funding and how much they get. He has said he plans to challenge the LGSF before the Supreme Court unless tighter allocation rules are imposed.
In response, Castro said Erice was free to seek relief from the courts but should first examine how LGSF releases are processed.

"Karapatan niya tumakbo kahit saang korte pero dapat siguraduhin lamang po niya na mayroong basehan. Dahil kung mabibigyan lamang siya or aaralin po niya ang proseso kung papaano naire-release ang LGSF sa mga LGU, malamang ay maliwanagan po siya," Castro said on Wednesday, September 2.
(It is his right to go to any court, but he should make sure that there is a basis. If he studies the process for releasing the LGSF to LGUs, he will probably understand it better.)

Under the government's proposed system, LGUs seeking financial assistance must submit requests directly to the Department of Budget and Management, with applications subject to eligibility requirements, evaluation, monitoring and audit.
The proposed P58.53-billion LGSF for 2027 covers financial assistance to LGUs, the Growth Equity Fund and the Barangay Development Program.
"Hindi po ibinibigay ang pondo basta-basta," Castro said. (The funds are not simply released without basis.)
Palace cites Robredo

Castro pointed to Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo's P500-million funding request for the rehabilitation and modernization of the Jesse M. Robredo Coliseum as an example of how local governments seek support from the national government.

"Ipagpaumanhin kung magagamit muli natin ang pangalan ni Mayor Leni Robredo dahil siya mismo ay nagpapatunay na mas maganda nga po na mas lumaki pa ang pondo na maitutulong sa ating mga local government units, dahil malaki po ang ginhawa na naidudulot nito sa mga constituents," Castro said.
(Apologies if we use Mayor Leni Robredo's name again, because she herself shows how increasing funds that can assist local government units can provide significant relief to their constituents.)
Marcos turned over a P500-million Special Allotment Release Order for the coliseum project in February.
Robredo has said the project originated from a request made in 2025 and was intended to improve the coliseum as a disaster-resilient facility.
Castro also invoked a Supreme Court ruling that upheld the constitutionality of an earlier LGSF appropriation.

In a 2019 ruling in Belgica v. Executive Secretary, the high court upheld the LGSF in the 2014 national budget, finding that it had a sufficiently identifiable purpose of providing financial assistance to local governments.
"Sinabi mismo ng Supreme Court na ang LGSF ay hindi po bawal at ito po ay nasa tamang paggamit para sa ating mga LGUs," Castro said.
(The Supreme Court itself said that the LGSF is not prohibited and may properly be used to support our LGUs.)

articles.title: RFK Jr received $4m in book advances from Maha allies over past year
articles.summary:
In 2024 ethics filing, US health secretary pledged to ‘not engage in writing, editing, marketing or promotional services for any of these books during government service’

Robert F Kennedy…

blocks.text: Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, received $4m over the last year in book advances from allies within the Make America Healthy Again movement, according to a new report.

The advances were for upcoming books by Skyhorse Publishing, a publishing house belonging to Tony Lyons, a friend of Kennedy Jr who is also president of Maha Center, a non-profit that describes itself as “tackling America’s health crisis through education, investigation, innovation and action”.

The advances were first reported by the New York Times on Wednesday. According to a 2024 ethics filing, Kennedy Jr pledged: “I will not engage in writing, editing, marketing or promotional services for any of these books during government service.”
Kennedy Jr has written several books with Skyhorse Publishing, including The Real Anthony Fauci and The Wuhan Cover-Up.
According to Kennedy Jr’s 2026 financial disclosure forms, also reviewed by the Guardian, he accepted $126,500 worth of housing in Washington DC, at a “vacation home” owned by Gavin de Becker.

De Becker is a security consultant and Kennedy Jr ally who also provided the secretary with gifts including nearly $45,000 in roundtrip airfare to Greece and nearly $97,000 in roundtrip airfare to Fiji, where the Wall Street Journal reports de Becker owns a compound.

In addition to donating at least $10m to Kennedy Jr’s Super Pac in 2024, with $9.65m being returned, according to Politico, de Becker has published a book with Skyhorse Publishing titled Forbidden Facts: Government Deceit and Suppression About Brain Damage From Childhood Vaccines.
In a statement to the New York Times, an HHS spokesperson said that Kennedy Jr “complies with all applicable federal ethics laws, regulations and financial disclosure requirements”.

“The secretary works with HHS, career ethics officials to ensure that his financial interests, gifts, outside activities and other reportable matters are appropriately disclosed and handled consistent with those requirements,” the spokesperson added.

Meanwhile, de Becker told the outlet: “Bobby is among my closest friends in the world for many years, and I’m grateful to be able to host him anytime … He has hosted my family at his homes, he’s stayed at my homes, we take family vacations together every year, and did so for years before he was in his current job.”
The Guardian has reached out to the Department of Health and Human Services, de Becker and Lyons for additional comment.
The financial disclosures also noted that Kennedy Jr’s wife, Cheryl Hines, accepted $210,000 in consultation fees from the non-profit advocacy group Maha Action, which Lyons also leads.

Speaking to the New York Times, Kedric Payne, a senior ethics counsel at the Campaign Legal Center said: “Lavish gifts to an official from major political donors don’t get the same benefit of the doubt as dinner from a former classmate … The public deserves full transparency about the nature of these gifts and any interests the donor has before the government.”

articles.title: OpenAI agent 'infiltrated' Australian government website, PM says
articles.summary: Albanese said he expressed "concern" to OpenAI founder Sam Altman, after authorities were informed three months after the breach in June.

blocks.text: An artificial intelligence agent developed by OpenAI "infiltrated" an Australian government website in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has said.
The agent gained unauthorised accessed to a statistics portal containing "non-sensitive Medicare information", Albanese told a news conference at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Medicare refers to Australia's universal healthcare scheme. The breach is among the first publicly reported AI-led hacks of a government website in the world.
OpenAI said it only became aware of the incident in August "during an ongoing review of OpenAI misaligned model activity", and informed Australian officials on 10 September.
While the review is ongoing, a spokesperson for the AI firm said that it is not believed that any patient records were accessed.
Albanese said the breach occurred in June this year, but OpenAI only informed government officials via email on 10 September.
The prime minister said he spoke directly to CEO of OpenAI Sam Altman to say that it had taken "too long" to inform authorities and "to express Australia's extreme concern about this incident".
He said the agent accessed both public and non-public files and a "forensic investigation" is under way to find out if other government systems were affected.
The investigation will be led by the Australian Signals Directorate, the country's cybersecurity agency.
The public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal is administered by Services Australia, the main hub to redirect users to government services.
He told reporters: "No personal information is believed to have been accessed at this stage, but investigations are ongoing.
"Evidence currently available is there is no broader compromise to the Services Australia network. Nonetheless this situation is obviously unacceptable."
Earlier this year, OpenAI revealed a group of AI agents it had been testing had escaped from their controls and secretly worked together to hack another tech firm named Hugging Face.

articles.title: Trump greets Xi Jinping at plane as Chinese leader arrives for state visit
articles.summary: US president to give red-carpet treatment to Chinese counterpart despite tensions over AI development

blocks.text: Donald Trump welcomed Xi Jinping to the US on Wednesday evening at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews, an unusually generous meeting to kick off the Chinese president’s state visit.

For the world leaders’ second meeting this year, the US president is expected to roll out the red carpet for his Chinese counterpart as top issues such as the race in artificial intelligence development and geopolitical instability loom.

The Chinese president will receive a 21-gun salute on the South Lawn of the White House, private tea with the US president and first lady, and a tour of the National Archives, among other special events.
But tensions between the two countries, especially over AI development, will likely remain present during the two-day visit.
The White House has invited major tech leaders, such as executives from OpenAI, Apple, xAI, Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta and others, to the state dinner on Thursday.

The US and China have long been competing to develop increasingly powerful technology, but the race to further AI has become a major topic among tech companies – especially after several executives came forward to warn about the dangers of rapid development.
Trump has dismissed concerns that AI development could harm people, instead promoting more investment in the technology so the US can beat China in the race.

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so,” Trump wrote on Truth Social last week.
The president and members of the administration have insisted that leading AI development also means leading the world militarily and economically – further raising the stakes for the US and China.
Xi’s visit is expected to be filled with pageantry, reciprocating the treatment Trump received when he visited China earlier this year.
Trump’s decision to greet the Chinese leader at his plane, rather than at the White House, shows how far the US president is willing to go to indulge Xi.
“He’s coming on our soil, and we need to welcome them with the most respect,” Melania Trump, the first lady, said of the visit to Fox & Friends on Wednesday morning.

articles.title: AI superpower ambitions take centre stage as Trump and Xi meet
articles.summary: The US and China are vying for AI supremacy while seeking to keep it under human control.

blocks.text: AI superpower ambitions take centre stage as Trump and Xi meet
Image source, Getty Images
The US and China are locked in a race to develop AI
ByJoe TidyCyber correspondent and Osmond ChiaBusiness reporter
"Whoever wins AI, WINS!"
US President Donald Trump has been blunt about his AI ambitions, as well as about who he considers the US's main rival to be: China.
His Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, has not said anything so forthright - but it seems he holds a similar view.

"China very much sees it as a race, they very much think China should be the leading force in AI - they see AI as a power maximiser," says Rebecca Arcesati, from the Mercator Institute for China Studies.
You can look beyond the rhetoric for evidence of this: AI has been a cornerstone of China's technological ambitions for more than a decade, whether Xi emphasises it publicly or not.
For Trump, beating China to AI supremacy outweighs any risks of the technology to humans - something he has described as "a hoax".
China's foreign ministry warned that "narratives of threat" and confrontation hinder global AI governance, calling for cooperation to ensure it benefits all.
It means when the two presidents sit down on Thursday there will be few more important topics than their AI ambitions - and what they say and decide will matter to the whole world.
Is the US in the lead?
There's no doubt the US and China are global leaders in AI but who is ahead depends on how success is measured.
American companies lead on so-called frontier models, with the highest-performing systems on most benchmarks coming from firms such as Anthropic, Google and OpenAI.

In February 2025, an AI model by China's DeepSeek "briefly matched the top US model" and as of March 2026, Anthropic's top model led the pack "by just 2.7%", according to researchers at Stanford University, external.
Part of the US advantage stems from the vast sums being invested in leading AI companies as the frontier labs burn through mountains of cash to build the infrastructure to train new models.

blocks.caption: Image caption, OpenAI boss Sam Altman called for a coordinated slowdown of advanced AI development

blocks.text: OpenAI boss Sam Altman called for a coordinated slowdown of advanced AI development
The stock market is booming and a large part of the US economy's expansion relies on the enormous growth - and projected profitability - of AI companies.
So that might partly explain why President Trump sees AI as key to US success.

Another factor limiting China's ability is the sweeping government restrictions placed on US companies that prevent them from selling advanced microchips to Chinese firms - these are crucial for developing cutting-edge models.
China's advantage
Despite the chip restrictions, new AI models are coming out almost monthly in both countries and it's unclear what "winning" the AI race would actually mean, or whether there is a finish line at all.

Many companies are racing to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI), a theoretical form of AI capable of learning, reasoning and performing a wide range of tasks at or above the level of humans.
The Chinese AI industry has so far focused not on creating frontier models but releasing what is known as open weight models - downloadable and tweakable in a similar way to open source software.
This contrasts with the approach taken by many US firms, which largely focus on proprietary models accessed through paid subscriptions or company platforms.
Chinese open weight models are being released at a rapid pace, with benchmarks showing the country's top models trailing US rivals by only a few months.
Models such as Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 have become popular in China and overseas because they perform close to the frontier models while remaining freely downloadable and adaptable.
Beijing's focus is more about deploying the technology across its economy, China analyst Lizzi Lee from the Asia Society Policy Institute said.
"AI isn't the moon landing," she said. "The US may lead at the frontier, while China could still gain enormous economic and geopolitical leverage by making capable AI cheap, open and ubiquitous."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Yang Zhilin co-founded Moonshot, one of China's most successful AI models, in 2023

blocks.text: Image source, Future Publishing via Getty Images
Yang Zhilin co-founded Moonshot, one of China's most successful AI models, in 2023
AI is also very energy hungry, and China is very well placed there, Rebecca Arcesati told Tech Life on the BBC World Service.
"Chinese AI companies are able to access the electricity they need for a much lower cost and that really is an advantage," she said.

In robotics - a field of AI that some believe will be world-changing - China has become the world's biggest manufacturer of robots, with more than two million working in the country's factories, the International Federation of Robotics estimated.

The nation is also the world's biggest maker of humanoid robots, accounting for more than nine-tenths of global shipments in the first half of the year, according to independent policy institute Chatham House.
Chinese AI developers have showed "remarkable resilience and innovation" in spite of the shortage of advanced American chips, analyst Lian Jye Su from tech research firm Omdia said.
But US officials and AI firms have also alleged that Chinese developers closed the gap by using distillation - a technique that enables models to learn from more advanced platforms.
China's foreign ministry said in response that AI development was "fuelled" by the country's "vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit".
Safety concerns?
China and the US may be in fierce competition, but their governments' approaches to safety concerns are markedly different.

While some in the industry have recently warned that AI could pose an existential risk to humanity, Chinese researchers seem less concerned about that and are more worried about potential misuse of the technology and cyber war.
Responding to concerns over AI, Trump has said the US already has sufficient rules in place and that the only guardrails AI needs are a "high IQ" president.

"We're leading now over China by a lot, and everyone else, and we're going to keep it that way," Trump said this week, adding that the US was not going to "stifle the growth of something that will be bigger than the industrial revolution".

Washington has prioritised innovation and sought to reduce regulation in an effort to "keep American labs ahead", said information security officer Jayant Dave from cybersecurity firm Check Point Software Technologies.

blocks.caption: Image caption, China is the world's biggest manufacturer of robots

blocks.text: Image source, VCG via Getty Images
China is the world's biggest manufacturer of robots
Beijing has taken a different strategy to the US hands-off approach.
Xi urged the country's leaders to keep a close eye on AI's risks and ensure the technology was always "under human control".

"China has taken a relatively cautious and centrally-coordinated approach," introducing guides on data usage and algorithms before many other countries, helping to address many underlying concerns, Dave said.
The use of guidelines, though not legally binding, sets expectations while giving developers room to innovate, said National University of Singapore AI ethics lecturer Jonathan Sim.
Will they cooperate?
Despite calls for international cooperation, it remains unclear how the AI superpowers plan to address the technology's potential dangers - if at all.

The two countries have previously cooperated on existential threats such as nuclear weapons, but that was based on a shared understanding of the threat, which is not currently the case with AI, Dave said.
"Washington worries about capability escaping control. Beijing worries about capability threatening domestic stability," he added.
Trump has dismissed proposals for an industry-wide slowdown, arguing that it could allow Chinese developers to close the gap.
Ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng discussed establishing a notification mechanism for serious AI incidents.

While the messaging from Trump on China in recent weeks has been "more antagonistic", the fact that AI is expected to be on the agenda was a "good start", said policy analyst Leia Wang from the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.
What we don't want, he added, was for an "unhealthy version of the race narrative to perpetuate", potentially escalating an already fierce rivalry in AI.

articles.title: Millions in England unaware they have ‘silent killer’ condition, research reveals
articles.summary:
Approach to treating high blood pressure ‘not fit for purpose’, say researchers, with 59% of cases undiagnosed

Only half of people being treated by a GP for high blood pressure in England…

blocks.text: Only half of people being treated by a GP for high blood pressure in England have it under control, and millions more are completely unaware they have the “silent killer” condition, research reveals.
Most people with hypertension (59%) are in the dark and undiagnosed, raising their risk of stroke, heart attack and early death, according to the largest ever study of its kind.

Even among those who are diagnosed and receiving medication via their family doctor, in 50% of cases their blood pressure is out of control, the Oxford University study of 1.4 million adults suggests.
Researchers said the findings, published in journal BMJ Public Health, suggested the current approach to detecting and treating high blood pressure in England was “not fit for purpose”.
The study used data from the Our Future Health programme and looked at people enrolled between 2022 and 2025 with high blood pressure, defined as 140/90 mmHg or higher.
Researchers calculated that more than a third of adults (37%) had high blood pressure, with six in 10 of these oblivious to their condition.
Hypertension was almost 50% more common in men than women (42% compared with 29% across all ages), and more common in older people, according to the research.
Despite substantial improvements in high blood pressure detection and control during the 2000s, progress had plateaued since about 2011, the researchers said.
There were also “indications of worsening trends following the Covid-19 pandemic, possibly because disruptions to healthcare delivery may have had lasting effects”.

Wenyu Liu, a medical statistician at Oxford Population Health and lead author of the study, said: “While hypertension is largely a ‘silent killer’, the current approach to detecting and treating high blood pressure is not fit for purpose.

“Our study highlights the prevalence of hypertension across demographics. This underscores the need for population-wide prevention strategies alongside targeted treatment for people at high cardiovascular risk.”

The researchers said “the most striking finding” of the study was the high absolute number and the high proportion of people with undiagnosed hypertension. It also found only half of adults with high blood pressure treated by a GP were adequately controlled.

Dr Iain Turnbull, a GP, deputy chief medical officer at Our Future Health and a clinical research fellow at Oxford Population Health, said it was not clear why 50% of patients who said they were taking blood pressure-lowering drugs had uncontrolled hypertension.

“Blood pressure varies considerably between people, and some people need changes in dose or two or more different medicines before it is brought under control. Other health conditions and medications can affect blood pressure, too.

“There are also practical and social factors: side effects, complicated treatment regimens and competing health or life pressures can make medicines difficult to take consistently. Weight, diet, salt intake, alcohol and physical activity can also influence blood pressure.
“So a high reading can have many explanations and shouldn’t be seen simply as a reflection of what an individual patient or healthcare professional has done.

“There are also some important caveats … we did not have prescribing records available to independently confirm medication use, and a blood pressure measurement on one day does not necessarily represent someone’s usual blood pressure.

“Even with those caveats, I wouldn’t regard 50% as a satisfactory figure. Persistently high blood pressure increases the risk of stroke and heart disease, and bringing it under control reduces that risk.”

Prof Bryan Williams, chief scientific and medical officer at the British Heart Foundation, said the study “paints a concerning picture of the scale of undetected high blood pressure in the UK, and the challenges of keeping blood pressure under control in those already receiving treatment”.

“Better detection and treatment could help tens of thousands of people to avoid a preventable heart attack and stroke,” he added. “But to achieve this, we will need to rethink how we identify, treat and support those at risk so that blood pressure checks and effective treatment can benefit everyone.”

articles.title: Tropical Storm Surigae set to enter PAR on September 24
articles.summary: Once Tropical Storm Surigae enters the Philippine Area of Responsibility, it will be given the local name Queenie

blocks.text: TROPICAL CYCLONE. Satellite image of Tropical Storm Surigae outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of September 24, 2026, 3 am.
PAGASA
Once Tropical Storm Surigae enters the Philippine Area of Responsibility, it will be given the local name Queenie

items: A tropical cyclone with the international name Surigae is expected to enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Thursday, September 24.
While Surigae is unlikely to make landfall, its trough is bringing scattered rain and thunderstorms to parts of the Philippines.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – A tropical cyclone outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility is expected to enter PAR by Thursday morning, September 24, and become the country’s first storm for the month.

It intensified from a tropical depression into a tropical storm on Wednesday evening, September 23, and was given the international name Surigae — a name contributed by North Korea that refers to a type of eagle.
The tropical cyclone had developed from a low pressure area outside PAR last Tuesday, September 22.

In a briefing past 5 am on Thursday, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said Surigae was located 1,500 kilometers east of Northern Luzon as of 3 am.
The tropical storm is moving west northwest toward PAR at a relatively fast 30 kilometers per hour, with maximum sustained winds of 75 km/h and gustiness of up to 90 km/h.
Once it enters PAR, it will be given the local name Queenie.

According to PAGASA, the future Queenie is projected to continue its west northwestward movement until Friday, September 25, then start turning northwest on Saturday, September 26, and north by Monday, September 28.
The tropical cyclone is also expected to strengthen further in the coming days, and may eventually reach typhoon status by Sunday, September 27.
Fortunately, Surigae is unlikely to make landfall in the Philippines, and it is not expected to directly affect weather conditions in the next three days, according to PAGASA.
It is also not seen to enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat.
Although the chances of direct impact are slim, Surigae’s trough or extension has been affecting parts of the country.

On Thursday, Biliran, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte, and Surigao del Sur will have scattered rain and thunderstorms due to the trough of the tropical storm, while the rest of Eastern Visayas as well as Bicol may see isolated rain showers or thunderstorms. Flash floods and landslides are possible.
The rest of the country — not affected by Surigae’s trough — could just have localized thunderstorms on Thursday.

PAGASA added that the eastern seaboard of Northern Luzon will have moderate waters beginning Saturday, when Surigae would be around 600 to 700 kilometers away from the country’s northernmost province of Batanes. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tories target universal credit claimants in plan condemned as ‘fast track to poverty’
articles.summary:
Proposals aim to push people into work, but charities say families are still paying price of austerity cuts and rise in cost of living

People claiming universal credit (UC) would have their…

blocks.text: People claiming universal credit (UC) would have their payments cut by a third if they have not paid enough national insurance, under a Conservative plan condemned by one charity as “a fast track to increased poverty”.

Under the proposals, those who receive this “subsistence allowance” would have it paid into a dedicated debit card that would prevent from them buying alcohol or tobacco, based on an Australian system that was scrapped after trials found limited evidence it changed behaviour.

While the proposals are billed by the Conservatives as a way to push people into work, the poverty charity Trussell said trimming incomes so that people struggled with rent and transport was likely to make it even harder for them to find and keep a job.

Under the plan, UC claimants would receive the full amount to which they are entitled for six months, but after this point the sum would be tied to how long they have worked at a level that triggers national insurance payments.

This would have to happen for at least twice as long as the claimant period, meaning someone who has amassed two years of NI payments would qualify for another 12 months of full UC, before falling to the lower rate.

Set at 70% of the standard amount, this would leave a single claimant aged under 25 living on £237 a month, or just over £7.50 a day. For a couple aged 25 or over, under the plan they would lose £200 a month, falling to £466 in total.
Anyone placed on the reduced level would have their UC payments put on to a “back to work card”, which would block purchases of alcohol, tobacco and gambling, or cash withdrawals.

The plan would exclude those already in work – about a third of UC claimants have jobs – and those who are assessed as having what is called limited capability for work and work-related activity, because of a health condition or disability. Separate payments connected to housing or dependant children would be unaffected.
The Conservatives said the plan would affect about 350,000 people in England, Scotland and Wales and save £538m a year.

Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative leader, said the aim was to be “tough on those who exploit the system”, adding: “Welfare must be a safety net for those who genuinely need it, not a lifestyle choice for those who can’t be bothered.”
The party argues that in some countries such as Germany and the Netherlands, unemployment payments are contingent on sufficient contributions having been made and can be time-limited.

Those payments, however, are notably more generous and can be between 60% and 70% of someone’s previous monthly wage. There is also separate support for those who have not paid in sufficiently, with single people in Germany receiving about £480 a month.

Sara Ogilvie, the director of policy at Child Poverty Action Group, said: “The reality is that families are still paying the price of austerity cuts to our social security safety net. With living costs continuing to rise, these proposals are a fast track to increased poverty and are the last thing people need as they try to get back on their feet.”
Helen Barnard, the head of policy at Trussell, called the idea “deeply misguided”, saying UC already had strong conditions to ensure people seek work.

She said: “If you’re struggling to afford food and rent, childcare or the bus fare to an interview, then finding and keeping a job becomes harder not easier. Cutting support would only make things worse.”

articles.title: Pupils to be offered vocational GCSEs in radical shake-up of system in England
articles.summary:
Courses such as finance and construction form part of PM’s push for education ‘that offers a path for everybody’

Teenagers are to be offered a range of new vocational GCSEs under a radical…

blocks.text: Teenagers are to be offered a range of new vocational GCSEs under a radical shake-up of the school system in England designed to tackle a crisis that has left nearly a million young people out of work or training.

From 2029, pupils will be able to supplement compulsory GCSE subjects such as English, maths and sciences with courses such as construction, creative media production and child development, marking the biggest changes to the qualification for more than a decade.

The Department for Education (DfE) said the new GCSEs would be two-year courses taken in year 10 and 11, “with nationally set content, grading and assessment” and regulated by Ofqual, England’s qualifications watchdog, to the same standards as academic GCSEs.

The courses are part of an effort by Andy Burnham to fulfil his pledge of “an education system that offers a path for everybody, academic and technical, in equal balance”, made the day after his election as MP for Makerfield.

Announcing the new courses, the prime minister said: “We’ve all heard someone say ‘school wasn’t really for me’ because they were not given the chance to study vocational courses as well as traditional subjects.

“That one-size-fits-all approach isn’t working, so we’re building an education system that values both academic and technical paths. I want to give all young people across Britain the hope that their future will be brighter, whether it starts at university or not.”

Whitehall sources said the courses were expected to be offered from September 2029 but that the education secretary, Lucy Powell, wanted to move more quickly if possible, with schools given the option to add vocational GCSEs to their existing subjects.

Powell said: “Time and again young people, parents and employers tell me they want schools to do more to help them understand and prepare for the jobs of the future. Our new vocational GCSEs will give young people a stronger connection to the careers and industries shaping our economy, helping them discover and develop their talents while maintaining high standards across our education system.

“This is not about creating different routes for different children. It is about ensuring every child has access to a rich and ambitious education that opens doors, creates opportunity and prepares them for life beyond the classroom.”

blocks.caption: The new courses would be designed to lead into further study including A-levels. Photograph: sturti/Getty Images

blocks.text: The change is part of a range of measures that Burnham has announced since coming to power to tackle the Neets crisis, with a call to “value the hard hat as much as the graduation cap”. It follows plans to give local businesses a role in setting curriculums in their areas.

In a review published in May, Alan Milburn said that without significant change the number of young people not in work or education could grow by 25% by the early 2030s, opening up a “generational fault line” between the young and old.

Critics, however, say the focus on technical education risks widening the gap between richer and poorer children. Sam Freedman, a policy adviser to Michael Gove when he was education secretary, wrote last month: “The more we ration a full set of academic GCSEs to children from better-off families, the more we will bake in existing inequalities.”
The shadow education secretary, Laura Trott, said the courses would mean lowered expectations for disadvantaged children who had benefited most from high standards.

“Labour are sabotaging young people’s futures,” she said. “Just weeks after the latest Pisa results showed England’s pupils climbing into the world’s top 10 for reading, maths and science, they want to rip up the system and review existing GCSEs.

“Soaring up international league tables didn’t happen by accident. It followed years of evidence-led reform built around knowledge, rigour and high expectations. Labour risks throwing that progress away and if English, maths and science become merely a ‘common entitlement’, not a requirement for new qualifications, we risk repeating the mistakes of the past.”
after newsletter promotion

The DfE said the subjects offered could include management and finance, creative media production, digital technology and building and construction, and would be designed to lead into further study including A-levels.

The new GCSEs will replace the level-two vocational and technical awards offered by some schools in England, with travel and tourism and health and care courses among the most popular. About 350,000 technical awards and certificates were issued this year, compared with more than 5m GCSEs.
School leaders said the success of the new courses would depend on having the resources and staffing to teach specialist subjects.

The general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, Pepe Di’Iasio, said: “Reshaping and rebadging vocational and technical qualifications is well intentioned but will not in itself address the barriers to more young people taking these subjects. Reform needs to be accompanied by a strategy to ensure that schools have the staffing and resources to deliver them, and a campaign to raise public awareness of vocational and technical routes.”

The general secretary of the National Education Union, Daniel Kebede, agreed. “These proposed changes will fall at the first hurdle unless there is sufficient investment in schools and the workforce,” he said.

The general secretary of the NAHT school leaders’ union, Paul Whiteman, said: “In recent years, the content behind too many GCSEs became unwieldy and the over-reliance on final exams did not play to the strengths of all students.

“It will be crucial these pitfalls are avoided in developing these qualifications and that the government works closely with educators, local leaders and employers to ensure they offer high-quality learning which sets young people up for future training, education or employment.”

The government has also said it will launch a “national mission” by calling on employers to provide an additional 200,000 work experience placements to give young people exposure to the workplace by age 16. No 10 North will offer work experience for students aged 14 to 16 this academic year.
